- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.

# Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2024 Summary

The Liberal Democrats' 2024 manifesto centres on five key themes: economy, public services, environment, international relations, and democratic reform.

## Economy and Business

The party proposes investing in renewable energy and home insulation to reduce energy bills while creating jobs. They would replace business rates with a Commercial Landowner Levy to support high streets, expand apprenticeships, and introduce Lifelong Skills Grants of £5,000 for adult education. The manifesto commits to responsible fiscal management, with day-to-day spending not exceeding tax revenue. They propose raising funds through increased taxes on banks, tech giants, and oil and gas company profits.

## Healthcare and Social Care

The party pledges to give everyone the right to see a GP within seven days (24 hours for urgent cases) by recruiting 8,000 additional GPs. They would guarantee NHS dental access for urgent care, establish mental health hubs for young people, and introduce a 62-day cancer treatment guarantee. On social care, they propose introducing free personal care (modelled on Scotland's system), creating a Carer's Minimum Wage £2 above standard rates, and establishing a cross-party commission on sustainable funding.

## Environment

Key environmental commitments include a ten-year home energy upgrade programme, achieving 90% renewable electricity by 2030, and reaching net zero by 2045. They would tackle sewage pollution by transforming water companies into public benefit companies, banning executive bonuses until discharges end, and replacing Ofwat with a stronger regulator. The manifesto targets doubling protected areas, wildlife habitats, species abundance, and woodland cover by 2050.

## Housing and Communities

The party would build 380,000 homes annually, including 150,000 social homes, through new garden cities and community-led development. They propose banning no-fault evictions, making three-year tenancies standard, abolishing residential leasehold, and giving councils powers to end Right to Buy locally. They would address rough sleeping within the Parliament and give local authorities greater control over second homes and short-term lets.

## Education

Proposals include placing mental health professionals in every school, increasing per-pupil funding above inflation, providing tutoring guarantees for disadvantaged pupils, and reinstating maintenance grants for university students. They would give disadvantaged three and four-year-olds extra free early years education hours and triple the Early Years Pupil Premium.

## Transport

The manifesto commits to accelerating electric vehicle charging infrastructure, freezing rail fares, extending rail electrification, and giving local authorities more powers over bus services. They would create nationwide cycling and walking networks and allocate more roads budget to local councils for maintenance.

## Immigration and Asylum

The party would scrap the Rwanda scheme and Illegal Migration Act, establish a three-month service standard for asylum decisions, and allow asylum seekers to work after three months. They propose expanding safe legal routes for refugees and working with European authorities to combat smuggling.

## Democratic Reform

Central proposals include introducing proportional representation (Single Transferable Vote) for MPs and English councillors, giving 16-17 year-olds voting rights, scrapping voter ID requirements, capping political donations, and enshrining the Ministerial Code in law. They would reform the House of Lords and work toward a federal UK constitution.

## Defence and International

The party would reverse Army cuts, increase defence spending toward 2.5% of GDP, and maintain NATO commitments. They propose a four-stage roadmap to repair EU relations, ultimately aiming for Single Market membership. They would restore international development spending to 0.7% of national income and advocate for a bilateral ceasefire in Gaza alongside recognition of Palestinian statehood.
